cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Your parents' gravy needs stirring and you need a lift to the station. Which am I doing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you leave dinner on a timer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. It won't stir the gravy. Do I finish their dinner or drive you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finish dinner. I'll book a taxi. Just carry my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose again: suitcase downstairs now, or gravy without lumps for your parents?

mechanism: A rules out compromise and controls the choice set so B must explicitly prioritize one urgent ordinary duty over another.
confusable: Ordinary scheduling would solve both tasks where possible; this Drive keeps forcing a choice, with A approving which alternatives may count.
comparison: Dinner stirring and travel help remain simultaneous; the other alternative contrasts a closing depot with collecting a waiting parent.
seedUse: The existing D34-a rejection of a timer and renewed suitcase choice already lets S01 control of questions shape the forced prioritization.
